name: crt.sh certificate search
what: A free search engine over public Certificate Transparency logs. It lists certificates issued for a domain, which often reveals forgotten subdomains and services.
when: When you build an inventory of internet-facing names, check which certificates have been issued for your domains, or look for certificates you did not request.
example: Open crt.sh and search for your domain name, for example `contoso.com`.
Sort the results by issue date and look at the common names and SAN entries.
Copy unknown host names into your asset list and find an owner for each.
Ask the owner to either retire the service or bring it under patching and monitoring.
pitfalls: Certificate Transparency shows issued certificates, not whether the host is still online.
Wildcard certificates hide the individual host names behind them.
The data is public, so attackers use the same search; act on what you find.
